This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner - Balveer Singh with a prayer to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Certioari for quashing the impugned First Information Report dated 15.01.2023, registered as Case Crime No.0032 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 427 IPC, at Police Station Mohanlalganj, District - Lucknow; with a further prayer to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the opposite party No.1 to 3 to not to arrest the petitioner in pursuance of the impugned F.I.R.
As per version of the F.I.R., the informant is working in the Indian Army.

1 Managing Director of the real estate company Reality Investment Solutions Pvt. Ltd.

The sale deed of the land measuring to 1500 Sq.Ft. was executed on 03.07.2018 by the farmer Ram Sajivan in favour of the wife of informant, namely, Smt. Mamta Sahu and the Plot No. D-126 was also mentioned.
After execution of the sale deed, the informant got the boundary wall on the land constructed.
However, after some months, accused-petitioner Balveer Singh demolished the boundary and the bricks were also removed.

When the informant inquired about the said incident,
accused Balveer told that the boundary of the plot was zigzag, that is why he removed the boundary and he would get the boundary wall re-constructed.

However, after waiting for several months,
when the boundary wall was not constructed, the informant again got the boundary wall constructed but this time one R.P. Yadav got the boundary wall of the informant demolished and told the informant that this land was not of Balveer.
When the informant told about the incident to the farmer Ram Sajivan, he replied the informant that he did not know about the land and it is the accused - Balveer who knows about the land.

When the informant could not get his land, he gave application at police station Gosainganj, District Lucknow where the accused Balveer sought some time but the informant made a complaint at IGRS portal, then the informant could know that the informant was cheated and the land does not belong either to the accused Balveer Singh or Ram Sajivan.
Then the informant has lodged present F.I.R. against the accused persons.
It has been argued by learned counsel for petitioner that petitioner has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any offence.
The F.I.R. has been lodged with malafide intention.
Infact co-accused R.P. Yadav @ Ram Parikh Yadav is the co-sharer in the land in dispute.
The sale-deed has been executed by the co-accused Ram Sajivan who is also the director of the company.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has further submitted that infact a dispute took place between the informant and co-accused persons and the petitioner has no concern with the dispute.
The allegations levelled against the petitioner are absolutely false, frivolous and baseless.
No offence is made out against the petitioner, hence, the impugned F.I.R. is liable to be quashed.
Learned A.G.A., on the other hand, opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel for petitioner and submitted that petitioner is named in the F.I.R. Petitioner is a serial offender.
He is habitual of committing such crimes.

There are six cases lodged against the petitioner at different police stations of the District which are of the similar nature, to which learned counsel for the petitioner states that he has given explanation of four cases in para 9 of the writ petition.
In the present F.I.R. also the petitioner is actively involved.
Learned A.G.A. further submits that alleged offence is serious in nature as petitioner is involved in duping so many of investors.

He further submits that impugned F.I.R. discloses a cognizable offence against the petitioner and, therefore,
the present writ petition is liable to be dismissed.

Having examined the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusing the impugned F.I.R., which shows that cognizable offence is made out against the petitioner and also considering the criminal antecedents of the petitioner, we are of the opinion that no interference is called for by this Court in its extraordinary power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the impugned F.I.R. or for grant of any interim relief to the petitioner.
The writ petition lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
